issues.body: `collect()` passes `run_started_at` to `decompose_run()`, and `decompose_job()` then computes `job.started_at - run.run_started_at`. GitHub's run `run_started_at` is the execution start, not the time the run was created/queued, so the initial workflow queue interval is absent whenever the normal API field is present. The fallback to a job's `created_at` is never used on ordinary live payloads. This contradicts the module header and rendered report, both of which define `wait` as queue time plus time blocked on `needs:`, and can understate the reported wait for every leg by the run-level queue delay.
issues.fix_hint: Anchor live runs at the run's `created_at` when computing queue-plus-dependency wait (and name the parameter accordingly), while retaining a clearly documented fallback for fixtures lacking it. Add a test with distinct run `created_at`, run `run_started_at`, and job `started_at` values that verifies the live collection path includes both the run queue interval and the later dependency delay. Alternatively, rename and document the metric as post-run-start dependency delay everywhere if excluding workflow queue time is intentional.
issues.title: Live wait measurements omit workflow queue time

verdict.summary: The inventory and its hermetic tests are generally well structured, and the supplied 56-test suite passes. However, the new `wait` metric does not implement its documented meaning: the live collection path anchors it at the workflow run's `run_started_at`, which excludes the workflow's queue interval. Since the report explicitly presents `wait` as queue time plus dependency blocking, this makes a steering column materially incomplete and requires correction before approval.
